M2L2 perception of movement parameter is poor and that M2L1 variability of movement parameter negatively impacts perception.
M2L2 hearing learners of ASL made more movement errors than other types of errors, and that they made more movement errors in response to sentences produced by a M2L1 learner than a native signer.
M2L2 perception of ASL movement errors is negatively affected by M2L2 variability in the movement parameter.

the phonological processing of ASL by M2L2s.
the phonological perception of ASL and the effects of M2L2 variability on the perception of ASL phonology.
the perception of phonological parameters in ASL and the impact of phonological variability in the input on the perception of phonology by M2L2 ASL learners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M2L2 movement perception is negatively impacted by the variability of movement in M2L2 signers and that this is a function of the learner’s proficiency level in ASL.
movement parameter perception errors are the most common and most detrimental in late M2L learners of ASL.
M2L2 ASL learners’ perception of movement is impaired.

M2L2 perception of the movement parameter is poor and is further exacerbated by M2L2 variability.
the movement parameter is a challenging parameter for late learners of ASL.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the phonological parameters of ASL can be used to characterize L2 learners’ perception errors.
M2L2 perception errors are not random and can be characterized by the types of errors that are made and the types of errors made by different proficiency learners.
the phonological parameters of ASL are not processed independently and that the perception of one parameter may affect the perception of others.
